title: Maintaining Trap Seal Integrity in Drainage Systems
description: Liquid trap seals prevent hazardous sewer gases from escaping into occupied spaces, but unvented drainage flow can ruin their function. When wastewater flows down a drain line without proper atmospheric venting, the moving slug of water creates a localized negative pressure zone behind it. This negative pressure acts like a siphon, pulling water out of the fixture's P-trap and breaking the liquid barrier. Professional plumbers install correctly sized vents according to governing plumbing codes, balancing internal pipe pressure so the trap seal remains intact after every discharge cycle.

Maintaining Trap Seal Integrity in Drainage Systems

Liquid trap seals prevent hazardous sewer gases from escaping into occupied spaces, but unvented drainage flow can ruin their function. When wastewater flows down a drain line without proper atmospheric venting, the moving slug of water creates a localized negative pressure zone behind it. This negative pressure acts like a siphon, pulling water out of the fixture's P-trap and breaking the liquid barrier. Professional plumbers install correctly sized vents according to governing plumbing codes, balancing internal pipe pressure so the trap seal remains intact after every discharge cycle.
